title: Integrating Universal Generative AI Platforms in Educational Labs to Foster Critical Thinking and Digital Literacy
extended_summary:
This paper examines how contemporary generative AI platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and related text/image/video tools can be used in education, not as autonomous tutors, but as objects of critical inquiry. The authors argue that because current GenAI systems can generate plausible but incorrect outputs, educators should design learning experiences that help students evaluate, compare, and question AI-generated content rather than accept it uncritically.

The main intervention proposed is an interdisciplinary laboratory model in which students create prompts on material they already know, submit those prompts to multiple GenAI systems, and then judge the outputs for accuracy, completeness, and conceptual depth. Students use rubrics to distinguish fully correct, partially correct, and incorrect responses. The paper also describes a pilot implementation in a General Astronomy course for non-science majors, where students interacted with text, image, and video GenAI tools to generate and critique content related to astronomy topics.

The population discussed is primarily undergraduate students at Borough of Manhattan Community College, with the pilot focused on non-science majors. The setting is a college classroom/lab environment, and the work was implemented across several cohorts over multiple semesters. The paper concludes that text-based GenAI tools currently have the most educational value for college-level learning because they can produce mostly accurate explanations, while image and video tools are better suited to creative or speculative tasks and are currently unreliable for scientifically precise instruction. Overall, the paper emphasizes critical thinking, digital literacy, and informed AI use rather than direct evidence that GenAI improves literacy or reading outcomes.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: General-purpose generative AI / large language model chatbots and multimodal GenAI platforms used to generate text, images, and video content.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper examines student interaction with general-purpose GenAI tools in an astronomy lab and compares outputs across platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, NightCafe, Bing Image Creator, Google ImageFX, Craiyon, InVideo, Kapwing, and Synthesia.

findings.finding_summary: The paper reports that the GenAI-integrated astronomy lab increased student engagement, initiative, and critical thinking for non-science majors. It notes that multiple student cohorts completed the lab over several semesters, that some students completed all components within the allotted two hours, and that many voluntarily extended work outside class and shared outputs online. No standardized literacy outcome or comparison group is reported.
findings.measure: Student engagement, initiative, critical thinking, voluntary continuation of work, and qualitative pedagogical impact

findings.finding_summary: The paper claims the lab supported digital literacy and GenAI literacy, and that students learned to craft better prompts, check AI answers, and evaluate output quality. These conclusions are based on descriptive observation rather than a controlled literacy assessment, and no reading-specific outcome is reported.
findings.measure: Digital literacy / GenAI literacy / prompt engineering and critical evaluation skills

findings.finding_summary: The paper states that students deepened comprehension of astronomy content and strengthened scientific reasoning by comparing chatbot outputs against known answers and identifying inaccuracies. Text-based GenAI was reported to answer over 90% of undergraduate-textbook-difficulty questions accurately, while image tools reportedly failed on college-level scientific content with error rates approaching 100%; these are descriptive claims without experimental effect estimates.
findings.measure: Accuracy of GenAI responses on course-content questions; conceptual understanding of astronomy/science topics

quality_tier_rationale: This is a descriptive, implementation-oriented paper with no control group, standardized outcome measure, or causal design. The paper itself explicitly notes the absence of rigorous experimental methods, so it does not meet stronger evidence criteria.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports potentially meaningful positive engagement and learning signals, but provides no effect sizes or direct causal evidence. Because the reported impacts are qualitative and unquantified, the strength of impact is unclear rather than demonstrably large.
